title: Why we roast on Wednesdays
summary: Not tradition, and not the roaster's day off. It is what the resting window does to a Saturday order.
body:
People assume the roast day is chosen for the roastery's convenience. It is chosen for the coffee's.

Espresso wants somewhere between seven and fourteen days off the roaster before it stops tasting of gas and starts tasting of itself. Most of our wholesale goes out on a Thursday and lands in a grinder the following week, which puts a Wednesday roast squarely in the middle of that window.

Filter is less fussy and would be happy on a Monday. But two roast days means two heat-up cycles, two clean-downs and two of everything else, and the coffee cannot tell the difference. So: Wednesdays.
